title: PID control and anti-windup
keywords: pid controller gain gains proportional integral derivative windup anti-windup antiwindup saturation clamp tuning oscillation overshoot
text: A PID controller computes command = P error + I sum(error dt) + D d(error)/dt, with error = desired - measured. P reacts to the current error (too high: overshoot and oscillation), I removes the remaining steady error (too high: windup and slow overshoot) and D damps motion but amplifies sensor noise. In control_toolbox, u_clamp bounds the output and antiwindup_strat (NONE, BACK_CALCULATION or CONDITIONAL_INTEGRATION) stops the integral from growing while the output is saturated. Tune P first, then D to damp, then a small I, at the real loop rate: a different rate changes how the same gains behave.
